updates.note: Tells Continental Wire the port is 'the front door for American crude going overseas'; traders treat a storm closure as a known seasonal risk.
Tells Continental Wire it has been a strong summer on the docks.
Tells Continental Wire surge 'is the part that kills people'; leave now while roads are open.
Tells Continental Wire registered riders should stay by their phones; others should call 2-1-1.
Confirms to Continental Wire the port is closed to inbound vessels under Port Condition Yankee.
Tells Continental Wire the surge lifted oil out of the channel and wind spread it; boom going out, wildlife hotline open.
Explains to Continental Wire how retreating surge carries floating oil across shallow bays.
Tells Continental Wire Brightwake's remote-maintenance credentials were used without authorization; every remote connection shut off; does not know who did it.
Tells Continental Wire the Coast Guard will not characterize findings until the investigation is complete.
General advice to Continental Wire on remote maintenance: know who can connect, review access, segment systems.
Tells Continental Wire that remote access 'has to be watched'; declines to discuss the utility investigation.
Tells Continental Wire the FAA issued a notice after pilot reports of GPS interference; crews have other ways to navigate.
Tells Continental Wire flights into the station continue on backup navigation; no impact to the relief mission.
Tells Continental Wire residents can drink the water again; apologizes that it took five weeks.
Confirms to Continental Wire that investigators located a transmitter in a parked vehicle believed to be the source of the GPS interference; no further comment.
Tells Continental Wire the FAA has received no new reports of interference.
Tells Continental Wire the sweep is complete and the channel is open; declines to describe the search or security measures.
Tells Continental Wire ships are moving and terminals are loading; it will take time to work through waiting ships.
Tells Continental Wire the market has 'learned twice in two months' what one entrance means for export capacity.
Tells Continental Wire registration is free and lists what to bring; 'We know people have waited a long time.'
Tells Continental Wire the Navy suspended the vendor pending a fuel quality review; the station has fuel from other sources; no impact to operations.
Tells Continental Wire all product Quellmar delivered met specifications; cooperating with the review.
Confirms to Continental Wire court-authorized activity at two business locations; no further comment.
Reached by Continental Wire by phone, said 'No comment' and hung up.
Tells Continental Wire 'Remote maintenance is a door into the ship'; operators should know who holds a key.
Tells Continental Wire Brightwake still has not turned remote access back on and supports the advisory.
Urges operators to read the advisory; will not discuss the open investigation.
Tells Continental Wire the filing 'speaks for itself'; its claims are allegations.
Tells Continental Wire the company 'did the work we were hired to do' and will respond through its attorneys.
Written statement to Continental Wire: product met specifications; company will respond in court.
Tells Continental Wire 'being ready for the weather is only part of the job'; port working with Coast Guard and federal partners.
Tells Continental Wire the gaps her analysis measured were exposed, not caused, by the storm; the test is whether door-to-door registration reaches those streets.
Tells Anchor & Rotor the depot wants mechanics who 'like to fix things and want to stay in this community'; encourages veterans and spouses to apply.
Tells Anchor & Rotor student aviators are flying and it is 'a routine summer'.
Tells Anchor & Rotor to expect heavier traffic near the station at school start and dismissal; squadrons on a normal schedule.
Tells Anchor & Rotor many depot employees do the school drop-off before they clock in.
Tells Anchor & Rotor it is too early to say where Rafael goes; use the holiday weekend to get ready.
Tells Anchor & Rotor there are no changes to station operations; families will hear from the chain of command if that changes.
Tells Anchor & Rotor aircraft are safe and the focus is on people: follow the evacuation order and check in on arrival.
Tells Anchor & Rotor the hangars are buttoned up and the workforce was sent home; nobody should come in until told it is safe.
Tells Anchor & Rotor squadrons are back and training; aware of earlier drone reports, working with authorities, no impact to operations.
Tells Anchor & Rotor the depot is getting back to full speed 'building by building'.
Tells Anchor & Rotor crews train for GPS interference; flights continue on backup navigation with no impact to the relief mission or station operations; cannot discuss the cause.
Tells Anchor & Rotor Navy teams are searching the channel 'carefully and methodically'; will not discuss the device or the search.
Tells Anchor & Rotor there is no impact to air station operations; will not discuss security measures.
Tells Anchor & Rotor anyone whose deposit information was changed without permission 'will be made whole'; log in, confirm bank details, set up extra verification, do not reuse passwords.
Tells Anchor & Rotor the Navy suspended the vendor pending a fuel quality review; fuel from other sources; no impact to operations or family services.
Statement to Anchor & Rotor: all product Quellmar delivered met specifications; cooperating with the review.
Tells Anchor & Rotor the Navy will cooperate with any review of emergency contracts.
Confirms to Anchor & Rotor the Navy directed a security review of its Texas air stations; will not discuss scope or timing.
Tells Anchor & Rotor there is no impact to operations; holiday leave, housing and family programs continue; does not discuss force protection.
Confirms to Anchor & Rotor the FBI executed court-authorized search warrants; no further comment.
Tells Anchor & Rotor the Navy will cooperate fully with investigators; vendor suspended since November; no impact to operations.
Tells Anchor & Rotor the Navy supports its federal partners; channel was swept and cleared in November; will not discuss the device, investigation or security.
Tells Anchor & Rotor the attribution does not change daily routines; no impact to operations; security review continues.
Tells Anchor & Rotor he has 'never been prouder of the people on this station'.
Tells Anchor & Rotor depot workers 'fixed the hangars and then went home and fixed their own houses'.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: 'We can't send a bus to a house we don't know about.'
KNCB (Spanish): took an evacuation-assistance card at the fair; has registered several clients but not yet her own family.
KNCB (Spanish): says the county's list and her penciled notebook of neighbors without cars should look more alike.
KNCB (Spanish): describes her commute (6:10 a.m. bus, downtown transfer, second bus): 'Si pierdo el primero, pierdo la mañana.'
KNCB (Spanish): 'God gave me a car and a loud voice' but she cannot drive a whole neighborhood out; that takes buses and a plan.
KNCB (Spanish): urges parents to confirm the school has a correct phone number and a backup contact; describes her street's phone tree.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: the seasonal outlook says how busy, not where; 'it only takes one storm.'
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: too early to say where Rafael will go; prepare this weekend.
KNCB (Spanish): says she will start calling everyone on her penciled binder list.

KNCB (Spanish): sends her street's group text with Nueces River gauge readings; 'the river tells you first.'

Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: emergency contract awarded without bidding because debris cannot wait; put debris at the curb, sorted.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: 'We're working around the clock.'
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: damaged pumps need replacement parts; temporary pumps limit capacity; keep boiling.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: stomach illness visits beginning to ease; keep washing hands and boiling water.
KNCB (Spanish): says her family waited days for help; first water and food came from Whitfield's fellowship hall.
KNCB (Spanish): 'Nobody should have to wait until someone remembers their street.'
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: about 40 accounts posted in coordination and linked to the lookalike aid site; she does not say who is behind them.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: repeats that no one is seizing homes and aid is not limited to wealthy neighborhoods.
Named by KNCB as one of the accounts that spread the false home-seizure claim.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: the state has requested Individual Assistance; assessments slowed by spill-zone limits, flooded roads and scale; no fee to apply.
KNCB (Spanish): says families without savings cannot wait on paperwork; the hall keeps handing out food.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: ships are moving again in part of the channel; the inner channel stays restricted for decontamination; the backlog will take time.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: the 40 containers booked before the storm are finally ashore about a month late; frustrated by the anchorage wait.
KNCB (Spanish): 'Better late than never, but late is late'; hub keeps its posted schedule.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: Zavala Elementary was never a shelter; confirm shelters through the county, 2-1-1 or designated broadcast stations.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: ER visits near normal except in low-income neighborhoods near the bay, still about 40% above normal.
KNCB (Spanish): says the hallway beds are gone but she still sees families who waited too long to come in; never discusses individual patients.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: confirms the transmitter was found in a parked vehicle; investigation ongoing; no further comment.
KNCB (Spanish translation): says the blast came off the port bow around 1 a.m.; he counted heads; two of his crew were hurt; visits Fontenot most days.
KNCB (Spanish translation): by phone from the hospital, broken arm and concussion; grateful to his captain and crew.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: Navy teams found a second device and rendered it safe; will not describe it.
Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: channel remains closed until the search is complete; boaters must respect the safety zone.
KNCB (Spanish): hub runs on a posted schedule; 'the storm left in a day, the need did not.'
KNCB (Spanish): volunteers sorting donations on her days off; 'They helped me first. Now it's my turn.'

Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: file and keep records; claims unpaid after 90 days can go to the Coast Guard's National Pollution Funds Center.
KNCB (Spanish translation): plans to file within days with his penciled trip notebooks; 'Zero days fished. That part is easy to count.'
KNCB (Spanish): checks her FEMA deposit details daily; hers were never changed; 'I check it like I check the stove.'
KNCB (Spanish): help desk at the hall now also helps people check deposit details on two borrowed laptops.

Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: asking how public money is spent is fair; the specific viral posts are false.
Named by KNCB as part of the second wave of posts claiming contractors are stealing aid.

Quoted by KNCB in Spanish translation: the county is reviewing the records.
